See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 272a.

Kedārakalpa
Texts bearing this name are classified below on the basis of details available in catalogues. First are placed mss. of which no detail is available; the second set of texts are those which are specified a. tantra in catalogues. The third set of texts are those about which the maximum amount of details is known. They represent the same text although in the catalogues they are assigned in the order of the majority of references to a. obscure purāṇa called variously Vikhyāda or Vikṣādha or Vidhvāntapurāṇa; the Śivapurāṇa; or the Nandī- [Page030-b] (ºĪśvara) purāṇa; an. described in these a. Śiva-Kārttika (ºkeya) saṁvāda (largest) or Devī-Īśvara saṁvāda, or Īśvara-Nandī saṁvāda.
The text assigned to Rudrayāmala (BORI. 11 of 1898-99) is not different; some of the mantras an. stotras here are said to have been taken from it; see Lz. 363. RASB. V. 4133.
The portions covered by these three sections an. three Saṁvādas form part of the same text that describes the great journey (mahāpatha) from Kailāsa an. beyond through Kedāra an. other shrines en route. See particularly RASB. V. 4133 an. the extensive extrs. given there.
Probably the first two sets of texts given a. unspecified an. tantra are identical with this.
There are yet three other groups mentioned a. (a. Purāṇa in general (b) a. from Padmapurāṇa (only one) an. (c) from Skandapurāṇa. Although there is no clue to identify these the last especially (Sk. purāṇa) may be the same a. the text assigned to Vikhyāda or Śiva or Nandī purāṇa described above.
